title: Feedback and Confirmation
summary: Feedback closes the loop so users know whether an action was accepted, processing or rejected; match the message to backend truth.

MUST.text: Acknowledge state-changing actions and distinguish queued, processing and completed.
Show success only after backend confirmation; otherwise show processing or queued.
Make the feedback perceivable (visual plus, where useful, assistive announcement).

SHOULD.text: Use undo for reversible low-risk actions when safer than confirmation.
Show feedback within 100 ms and keep it visible long enough to read (≥3 s for toasts).

AVOID.text: Do not show success before backend confirmation.
Do not overuse confirmation dialogs for reversible, low-risk actions.

EXAMPLE.good: "After archive, status reads 'Archived' with Undo for 8 s; Undo truly restores."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Toast says 'Done' before save completes, with no undo."

FAILURE_MODES: Premature success messages hide failures and break trust.
Missing undo forces heavy confirmation dialogs for trivial actions.
Feedback that disappears too quickly is missed by slow readers and screen readers.
